directorMomentFloor.citation: Owner answer 1, October 9, 2026: the smallest adult row of the Holmes and Rahe Social Readjustment Rating Scale, 'Minor violations of the law', 11 life-change units divided by 100. Holmes, T. H., and Rahe, R. H. (1967), Journal of Psychosomatic Research 11(2):213-218.

spread.citation: Smallest adult row ('Minor violations of the law'): 11 units on the 1967 Holmes and Rahe scale, 22.14 in the 2021 replication (Wallace and others 2023). The floor and the interrupt line move together or not at all (data/research/stand-in-figures-2026-10-12.json).

directorInterruptImpact.citation: Owner ruling on answer 2, October 9, 2026: the scale's anchor event, 'Marriage', 50 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), so losing a household's only pay takes over the screen.

spread.reason: A pacing choice by the owner, not a quantity any study measures; the marriage anchor is 50 life-change units in both the 1967 scale and its 2021 replication (Wallace and others 2023), so the line does not move if the scale is updated.

directorScaleFeeling.citation: Identity: the core's appraised event impulses are already expressed on the life-change scale divided by 100 (src/core2/emotion.ts appraiseEvent).

directorFeelingSignals.citation: The core's appraisal carries an event's size on two signals, mood and stress (src/core2/emotion.ts appraiseEvent); the drives package puts the same life-change share on each (src/core2/modules/health.ts severityImpulse). Averaging the two returns that share.

directorWeightTieSociability.citation: The October 8, 2026 design's trait tilt at full strength (one quarter), reused for sociability on the tie channel. No direct source.

directorWeightMoneyRisk.citation: The October 8, 2026 design's trait tilt at full strength (one quarter), signed so that a person who avoids risk weighs a money loss more. No direct source.

directorMemoryRecentDays.citation: No study sets how long a person keeps every moment in full. A season (91 days) keeps the recent past whole for scenes, callbacks and the journal; older moments keep only the strongest by hindsight. Checked by a watched person's stored moments staying about the same size across a year (P15 two-level population).

directorMemoryKeptMoments.citation: No study sets how many older moments a person keeps one by one. Two a month over a year, matching the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's twelve-month window (Holmes and Rahe 1967); the rest stay as monthly summaries and as each pair's summed impact. Checked by stored moments staying about the same size across a year.

directorFilingImpact.citation: Filing to run for office, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Outstanding personal achievement', 28 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), the same scale the director uses for every life event.

directorVolunteerOfferImpact.citation: An offer of help at its full weight (a close tie, in a candidate's first small local race), scaled by the offer's own weight (offerWeight in src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts: the race's size, the candidate's earlier campaigns and the tie). At full weight it is over the interrupt line (0.5) and stops the day as a scene; a stranger's offer in a first council race sits near filing to run (0.28) and waits its turn among the year's moments; an offer in a statewide or presidential race is a journal line (owner, Oct 27, 4 PM Eastern: volunteers stop the player only when they matter, in small local races or a first campaign).

spread.citation: From just at the interrupt line to near a close friend's death (Holmes and Rahe 1967, 37 to 63 units); checked by src/director/volunteer-offer-weight.test.ts.

directorCampaignSpeechImpact.citation: Speaking to a campaign crowd, sized like hearing back from a town office (0.15): no Social Readjustment Rating Scale item covers it (Holmes and Rahe 1967), and it sits below filing to run (0.28) so it reaches the candidate's journal without interrupting play (interrupt line 0.5). Checked by the stop appearing as a scene for a campaigning candidate in a played year.
directorCampaignSpeechImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967), no matching item; spread 0.05 to 0.28

directorCampaignGiftImpact.citation: A gift that is everything others have given a campaign, sized like filing to run (0.28), and scaled by the gift's share of what others have given the campaign, so a first or large outside gift is a moment for the candidate and a small late one falls under the moment floor (0.11). No Social Readjustment Rating Scale item covers it (Holmes and Rahe 1967). Checked by a donor's gift firing the donor's ask in a played campaign.
directorCampaignGiftImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967), no matching item; spread 0.15 to 0.35

directorOfficeReplyImpact.citation: Hearing back from a town office about one's cause. No Social Readjustment Rating Scale item covers it (Holmes and Rahe 1967); sized below filing to run (0.28) and the scale's smallest civic items, so it reaches the person's journal without interrupting play (interrupt line 0.5). Checked by the reply appearing as a journal line in a played year.
directorOfficeReplyImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967), no matching item; spread 0.05 to 0.28

directorKinMovedImpact.citation: Someone close moving away, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Son or daughter leaving home', 29 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), reaching those tied to the movers by how much they matter to them.

directorEvictionImpact.citation: Losing one's home to eviction, sized like losing one's job (the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Fired at work', 47 life-change units divided by 100; its nearest item, 'Foreclosure of mortgage or loan', 30, understates it per Desmond and Kimbro 2015, Social Forces 94(1):295-324), the same size the drives engine gives an eviction.
directorEvictionImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967); Desmond and Kimbro (2015); spread 0.3 to 0.47

directorHomeLostImpact.citation: Losing one's home (doubled up with kin, in a shelter or on the street), the same size the drives engine gives it (driveHomeLostImpulse) and an eviction (directorEvictionImpact): Holmes and Rahe (1967), 'Fired at work', 47 life-change units divided by 100.

directorHomePurchaseImpact.citation: Buying a home, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Mortgage over $10,000', 31 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967).

directorBusinessFoundedImpact.citation: Starting a business, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Business readjustment', 39 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967).

directorBirthImpact.citation: A child born into the family, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Gain of new family member', 39 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), reaching the parents fully and others tied to them by how much they matter.

directorChargedImpact.citation: Being charged with a felony, sized between the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Minor violations of the law' (11) and 'Jail term' (63) life-change units, divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967).

directorConvictedImpact.citation: A guilty verdict, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Jail term', 63 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967); a verdict to probation alone weighs less in life but is read the same until the scale is split.

directorAcquittedImpact.citation: Acquittal at trial, sized like the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's nearest relief item, 'Marital reconciliation', 45 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967).

directorJailTermImpact.citation: A jail term, the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Jail term', 63 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), reaching those tied to the person by how much they matter.

directorReleasedImpact.citation: Release from prison, sized like the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Marital reconciliation', 45 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967): a return to the household after a separation.

directorElectionResultImpact.citation: Winning or losing one's own race, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Outstanding personal achievement', 28 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), the same item filing to run uses, and giving an inaugural address; the owner rules that running, winning and losing are journal entries (Oct 14).

directorChoicesPerTurn.citation: Owner ruling, Oct 14, 2026 (afternoon, docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md): a conversation always offers four replies ranked by the engine, with 'say nothing' a smaller control beside them, never one of the four.

directorFarewellWordings.citation: How many wordings of a parting word the conversation tries to find one not already said in the talk. The words bank holds a handful of farewells per register, so four tries reach one that is new in nearly every talk; checked by the repetition guard on a played year's talks.

spread.citation: Fewer repeats a farewell sooner; more only costs a few extra lookups.

directorFarewellWordings.estimatedFrom: The size of the parting-word bank in data/english/parts: a handful of wordings per register, so four tries reach one not yet said; spread 2 to 8

directorTalkRecentDays.citation: Owner, Oct 14, 2026, night: a talk starts from the biggest recorded event of either person, and someone not in the room is asked after only when something recorded happened to them. How long ago an event still counts as news between two people: one season.
directorTalkRecentDays.spread: 30 to 180 days, checked by reading the talks of a played year (src/director/conversation.test.ts)

directorTalkAddressDays.citation: The President's address is the day's news for a couple of weeks after it is given, counted from the day it was given, not from the day a person first heard of it: in play (Gilbert, West Virginia, Oct 28, 2026) people met in March still opened with "Did you catch the President's speech?" because they were filled in that day. Owner, Oct 27: scenes and talks read what is happening in the world now.
directorTalkAddressDays.spread: 7 to 30 days, checked by reading the talks of a played season (src/director/conversation.test.ts)

directorTalkSeenLittleDays.citation: The fewest days since two people last spent time together for "Haven't seen much of you since ..." to fit: in play (Amanave, American Samoa, Oct 29, 2026) a household member said it of yesterday. A week is when Americans say they have not seen much of someone they live with or know; a reading of the line, not a measured quantity.
directorTalkSeenLittleDays.spread: 3 to 14 days, checked by reading the household talks of a played month (src/director/household-quiet.test.ts)

directorTalkAddressImpact.citation: Owner, Oct 14, 2026, night: public news comes up only for people who follow politics closely. The President's address weighs as a talk's topic as this impact times the speaker's political engagement (src/core2/modules/views.ts), so it leads only for the engaged and only when no bigger event of their own does; kept small so a life event of their own (a job, a move, a birth) leads first.
directorTalkAddressImpact.spread: 0.1 to 0.3, checked by reading the talks of a played year

directorFloorVoteImpact.citation: A floor vote on a bill a member sits in, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Change in responsibilities at work', 29 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), the scale the filing and election impacts use.

directorExecutiveActionImpact.citation: A bill signed or vetoed reaches its sponsor at the size of the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Outstanding personal achievement', 28 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967); a veto falls between that and 'Trouble with boss' (23).

directorRecallImpact.citation: A recall petition against an official, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Trouble with boss', 23 life-change units divided by 100 (Holmes and Rahe 1967), a public dispute with those one answers to.

directorLawLearnedImpact.citation: Learning why one's own check or estate shrank: sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Change in financial state', 38 life-change units, scaled to a news item's share (about 0.3 of it) because the person only learns the cause of a change already felt (Holmes and Rahe 1967); below the interrupt line (0.5) so it reaches the journal and can become a scene without interrupting play.
directorLawLearnedImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967), item 'Change in financial state'; spread 0.05 to 0.2

directorPublicCommentImpact.citation: A resident standing up to speak at a public meeting before a vote. No Social Readjustment Rating Scale item covers it (Holmes and Rahe 1967); sized like an officeholder's act (0.15), below filing to run (0.28), so it reaches the speaker's journal and can become a hearing scene without interrupting play (interrupt line 0.5). directorPublicCommentImpact.estimatedFrom: Holmes and Rahe (1967), no matching item; spread 0.05 to 0.28

directorVictimizedImpact.citation: A crime against one's household or oneself, sized as the Social Readjustment Rating Scale's 'Change in living conditions', 25 life-change units divided by 100, up to 'Personal injury or illness', 53, for a robbery or an assault (Holmes and Rahe 1967, J Psychosom Res 11(2):213-8; the scale has no crime item). It reaches the people the crime engine's record names.

journalRaceCloseMargin.citation: Words judgment: a winner's lead over the runner-up of five points or fewer of the votes cast is a close race in a journal.

spread.unit: lead over the runner-up, as a share of votes cast
spread.citation: A judgment band for how a journal says a race went, to be checked against published margin-of-victory analyses of U.S. elections (Ballotpedia's state legislative ones bucket races at 10 points or fewer and at half a point or fewer); not yet sourced here.

journalRaceWideMargin.citation: Words judgment: a winner's lead over the runner-up of fifteen points or more of the votes cast is a race that was not close in a journal.

spread.unit: lead over the runner-up, as a share of votes cast
spread.citation: A judgment band for how a journal says a race went, to be checked against published margin-of-victory analyses of U.S. elections (Ballotpedia's state legislative ones bucket races at 10 points or fewer and at half a point or fewer); not yet sourced here.

settingHours.note: When a scene's setting can hold it, by the setting kind (situation-types.json settings), in minutes after midnight: a scene measured at the day's close stops the player's clock at the next minute its setting is open, never at midnight in a bedroom or an office (owner, Oct 27, 4 PM Eastern: no scene at midnight in an open office). A null opening is the controlled person's own day start (the core's playerDayStartMinute). One row per kind of setting, never per place.
settingHours.citation: Ordinary American hours by kind of place: a household awake from its morning to about 10 PM; visits and calls in the daytime and early evening; offices and workplaces on a daytime shift; local councils and boards often meeting in the evening; schools in a school day.
settingHours.spread: Openings 6:00 to 10:00 AM and closings 3:00 to 11:00 PM by kind; checked against the American Time Use Survey's share of people at home, at work and in public places by hour.

interruptStop.citation: The story director's stored moment: its impact, measured from the change on each channel and sized by the person's traits, is at or over the interrupt line, the Holmes and Rahe (1967) marriage anchor of 50 life-change units divided by 100 (owner ruling, October 9, 2026; CTO ruling on at-or-over, October 10, 2026).
